comment: `&` and `,` are the same separator in a `| class context, spelled two ways, and the analyzer read only one. The proof they are one construct is the child shape, identical with the token swapped: `| == a` -> `!| operator_compare type_variable` against `| == a & UList a` -> `!| operator_compare type_variable !& constructor type_variable` (clean-stdlib/StdOverloadedList.dcl:5,8). So `readClassContext` published the first conjunct of an `&`-joined context and dropped the rest — missing edges, not a missing label. Measured (validation/m14/fixtures/clean/ampersand-context-probe.mts): 1,995 class_context nodes at WIDE, 365 carrying an `&`, and the dropped conjuncts split 249 that would ADD a row against 264 that name a class already published on that same line (`| toReal a & toReal b & toReal c`, Clyde/Clyde/timeprofile.icl:337); at TRACKED the split is 62 / 47. The 264 are not a doubling, and the reason is `pushRel`'s key rather than a judgement made here: it collapses on `source|type|target|line`. Measured as an A/B on TRACKED (references-duplicate-probe.mts), `,`-only gives 10,049 edges / 9,570 distinct groups / 387 groups with more than one, and `,`-and-`&` gives 10,108 / 9,629 / 387 — the duplicate count identical per discriminator, so the fix adds 59 edges and 59 new groups and changes nothing about duplication. The label stays `references` for the reason given in instance-member-signature-context: a dictionary requirement is a type the member needs, not a supertype.

expectRelationships.comment: THE TARGET ROW. `both :: !Int !Int -> Bool | Eq Int & Ord Int` published only `Eq` before the fix; `Ord` is the conjunct the `,`-only reader dropped
the conjunct that was always read. Kept so a regression that drops the FIRST conjunct is caught here as well as the second

the MIDDLE conjunct of `| Eq Int & Ord Int & Size Int`. A reader that kept only the first conjunct and a reader that kept only the last BOTH miss this row, which is what makes it the discriminating case rather than another copy of line 36
the third conjunct, to pin the chain is read to its end and not truncated at two
`constraintName` reads an `operator_compare` leaf as a class name; this row keeps the operator path alive in FIRST position

the conjunct AFTER an operator class. `| == Int & Ord Int` is the corpus shape from StdOverloadedList.dcl:8, and it is the row that would break if the separator reset were keyed on the class name rather than on the child
a where-LOCAL signature inside a function body, joined by `&`: one scope deeper than module level
the INSTANCE's own context, `instance Ord Int | Eq Int & Size Int`, anchored on the instance line and sourced from the instance target `Int`
an INSTANCE MEMBER's own signature joined by `&`. This is the scope pass 4 fixed for `,`; the `&` spelling reached the same code by the same route and has to survive the same per-node signature index

THE CONTROL. `comma :: !Int !Int -> Bool | Eq Int, Ord Int` is `both`'s own constraint pair in the spelling that was always read. If this row disappears the `,` path regressed, which the `&` rows alone cannot detect

THE CONTROL with no separator: `single :: !Int -> Bool | Eq Int`. An implementation that reset `expectName` on every unnamed child — including the leading `|` — would republish `Eq` from the wrong child or stop reading single-constraint contexts entirely
a `declared_type` from the same signature, to show the context fix did not disturb type reading on the same line

THE REPEATED-CONJUNCT ROW. `repeated :: !Int !Int -> Bool | Ord Int & Ord Int & Size Int` names `Ord` twice in three conjuncts. `pushRel` collapses on `source|type|target|line`, so this is ONE edge, not two — and the corpus shape is real: 264 conjuncts at WIDE and 47 at TRACKED name a class already published on their line (`| toReal a & toReal b & toReal c`, Clyde/Clyde/timeprofile.icl:337)
the third conjunct, proving a repeated conjunct does not stop the chain being read to its end. A reader that stopped at the first repeat would publish `Ord` and lose `Size`

expectRelationshipCount.comment: THE DEDUPE ROW. Three conjuncts, two distinct classes, and `Ord` appears twice — so exactly 1 edge. A per-conjunct publisher gives 2 and fails here. This is the duplicate-vs-multiplicity question the previous round left open, pinned as a number
the same signature's second distinct class, also exactly 1
exactly one. A `&`-aware reader that also counted the separator token as a constraint, or that walked the context twice, would publish 2
exactly one. The duplicate-vs-multiplicity case measured 0 times in 2,181 files, so no correct implementation may produce 2 here — and this row is what would catch one that did
the `,` spelling stays at one edge per conjunct, so the two spellings are counted by the same rule rather than one of them being special-cased into doubling

forbidRelationships.comment: the negative control: `single :: !Int -> Bool | Eq Int` constrains on one class. An edge to `Ord` would be an invented constraint, and inventing a constraint is the same class of error as dropping one
`comma` names two classes. `Size` is in no context on that line, so nothing may be invented for it
`both`'s context is `Eq Int & Ord Int`. `Size` belongs to `three` and to the instance, and a reader that leaked a context across signatures would publish it here
the ruled type. Nothing in this file may produce one — see script/m14/clean-ruled.ts. A dictionary requirement is not a supertype relation, and joining two of them with `&` does not make one
`implements` belongs to the INSTANCE (`Int -> Ord`), never to a function whose signature carries a constraint
an instance MEMBER is not the instance. `implements` for this file is the `Int -> Ord` row at line 70 and nothing else
naming a class in a type position is a reference, not a call. The one call `three` makes is `size` at line 42
a dictionary requirement is a reference to a class, never a construction of one
`overrides` pairs a member with its class's member of the same name. `three` is a function, not a member, and this file's only overrides are the instance member at lines 72 and 73
two sibling classes are not nested. `contains` here is module->class and class->member only
